15# GCU400 specialization of ``aten::_philox_normal_``. 

16# 

17# The generic launch fixes BLOCK=512 and a 1D grid of cdiv(N, BLOCK*4) 

18# programs, which overflows the 65535-program grid.x hard limit of this 

19# backend for the 2**30-element benchmark shapes (grid = 524288 -> 

20# ``OutOfResources: out of resource: grid.x``). This copy keeps the ATen 

21# semantics bit-exact (the accuracy suite compares against a NumPy 

22# re-implementation of ``PhiloxDistribution.cu``, so the Philox-4x32-10 

23# chain and the Box-Muller pairing must not change) and reworks only the 

24# launch shape and the store path, following the sealed ``_philox_uniform_`` 

25# recipe (job j20261118014844_ae36db10): 

26# 

27# * One persistent grid-stride kernel covers the whole tensor with at 

28# most 24 programs, so the grid never depends on the problem size and 

29# the grid.x cap is structurally unreachable; small tensors keep the 

30# one-block-per-program shape where the persistent loop would cost 

31# ~0.4us at the launch floor. 

32# * The 32-bit counter fast path is selected by a runtime scalar branch 

33# inside the kernel (the (seed, offset) pair lives in a device tensor; 

34# reading it on the host would sync every call): when 

35# ``offset + total_counters <= 2**32`` and ``n < 2**31`` the counters 

36# and the flat offsets stay in uint32; otherwise the generic 64-bit 

37# counter math runs (large offsets, e.g. ``2**40``, stay exact). 

38# * EVEN drops the store masks when ``n % (BLOCK * 4) == 0``. 

39# 

40# 2026-11-19 perf round (job j20261119095120_6bf3d448, re-landed and 

41# re-validated by j20261119114750_51048f30, FMW-1619 P3): 

42# * Ablation at fp32/2**24 attributed the sealed uniform-family config 

43# (BLOCK=2048/48 programs/nw4, 222.9us) to ~45% stride-4 masked 

44# scatter stores, ~23% Philox, ~13% Box-Muller (the tops_log/sin/cos/ 

45# sqrt intrinsics are cheap) and re-swept the launch shape for the 

46# compute-heavier Box-Muller mix: BLOCK=1024 / 24 programs / num_warps=4 

47# wins every dtype and size (fp32/2**24 187.4us -17%, fp16 185.2us, 

48# fp32/2**30 11.05ms, fp16 11.39ms). The small path moves to 

49# BLOCK=512 / num_warps=2 (4.2-4.3us at n=4096, was 5.7-5.9us). 

50# * PACK2 (two 16-bit samples per uint32 store) is REMOVED: at the new 

51# sweet spot the packing shifts/orcs cost more than the halved store 

52# count saves (fp16/2**24 plain 185.2us vs packed 208.0us; fp16/2**30 

53# 11.39ms vs 12.86ms), unlike the uniform_ sibling where PACK2 paid 

54# off -- the Box-Muller arithmetic hides less of the store queue. 

55# * Rejected variants (kept out on purpose): 

56# - int32 store indices (``base = idx * 4`` on an int32 lane vector): 

57# 3.6% faster at 2**24, but the byte address silently wraps at the 

58# 2**31-byte span, so fp32 x 2**30 leaves elements >= 2**29 unwritten 

59# (NaN tail) and can fault with the P16 Sip-error abort depending on 

60# where the wrapped address lands. The uint32 counter form keeps 

61# 64-bit scatter addressing (``tops_masked_scatter64``) and is the 

62# only safe layout; see compiler_problems/P17 

63# sources/flaggems_enflame_philox_normal_i32_scatter_2p31.md. 

64# - ``tl.interleave`` contiguification of the four outputs: 20x slower 

65# (4.58ms vs 226us at fp32/2**24) -- the GCU layout conversion is a 

66# general shuffle, not a free register permute. 

67# - u64 packing of two fp32 samples (stride-2 scatter): 233.7us vs 

68# 226.4us, the 64-bit pack arithmetic outweighs the halved scatter 

69# count. 

70# 

71# The Philox chain itself stays on ``tl.philox``: a hand-written round that 

72# shares the 32x32 products probed no faster at BLOCK=1024 (332.4 vs 

73# 317.4 us at 2**24 fp32) and the u32-carry offset variant exposed a 

74# device-level fault axis (Sip exception -> KMD abort at fp32 x 2**30, see 

75# compiler_problems/P16 sources/flaggems_enflame_philox_normal_.md), so 

76# both were rejected in favor of the sealed uniform-family counter scheme. 

77# 

78# Host contract (2026-11-12 ruling): the wrapper only validates arguments, 

79# allocates the staging buffer for non-contiguous outputs and launches these 

80# kernels; no aten compute op is called. 

81# 

82# This module also publishes itself over the generic package attribute 

83# ``flag_gems.ops._philox_normal_`` (the same vendor-injection pattern as 

84# ``conj_physical`` / ``glu_backward_jvp``): SpecOpRegistrar rebinds the 

85# top-level ``flag_gems._philox_normal_`` and the aten registration, but 

86# the perf benchmark resolves the op through the submodule attribute, which 

87# otherwise keeps pointing at the generic implementation -- the one whose 

88# grid computation cannot run the core shapes at all.

90import logging 

91 

92import torch 

93import triton 

94import triton.language as tl 

95 

96from flag_gems.runtime import torch_device_fn 

97 

98logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) 

99 

100# `aten::_philox_normal_` is part of PyTorch's stateless Philox RNG family, 

101# which landed upstream after the 2.10 release. Builds that predate it ship no 

102# schema for the operator, and FlagGems' registrar refuses to install an 

103# implementation for an unknown schema. Define the upstream signature verbatim 

104# when it is missing so the operator can still be registered and exercised; 

105# on newer torch builds the guard short-circuits. 

106_PHILOX_NORMAL_SCHEMA = ( 

107 "(Tensor(a!) self, Tensor key, float mean=0, float std=1) -> Tensor(a!)" 

108) 

109 

110 

111def _ensure_philox_normal_schema(): 

112 if hasattr(torch.ops.aten, "_philox_normal_"): 

113 return 

114 try: 

115 torch.library.define("aten::_philox_normal_", _PHILOX_NORMAL_SCHEMA) 

116 except Exception as exc: # pragma: no cover - depends on the torch build 

117 logger.warning("Unable to define aten::_philox_normal_: %s", exc) 

118 

119 

120_ensure_philox_normal_schema() 

121 

122# Launch ladder (do_bench kernel mode, median w1000/r100, GCU400/L600): 

123# below 16K elements every configuration sits at the ~4.2us launch floor, so 

124# the one-block-per-program shape wins; from 2**24 elements on, persistent 

125# grid-stride with BLOCK=1024 / 24 programs / num_warps=4 is the Box-Muller 

126# sweet spot (2026-11-19 re-sweep of the uniform-family ladder: the heavier 

127# per-counter arithmetic moves the optimum away from BLOCK=2048/48 programs, 

128# and 24 programs also leave the scatter queue uncontended). 

129_SMALL_MAX_NUMEL = 1 << 14 

130_SMALL_BLOCK = 512 

131_SMALL_NUM_WARPS = 2 

132_PERSIST_BLOCK = 1024 

133_PERSIST_NUM_PROG = 24 

134_PERSIST_NUM_WARPS = 4 

135_F64_BLOCK = 512 

136_MAX_GRID_X = 65535

139@triton.jit 

140def _box_muller_f32(r0, r1, r2, r3): 

141 """Pair four Philox words into four standard normals, in float32. 

142 

143 Mirrors ``box_muller_float`` from cuda/PhiloxDistribution.cu: each word 

144 becomes a uniform in (0, 1] through the fused multiply-add 

145 ``fmaf(word, 2**-32, 2**-33)``, odd-indexed words turn into angles and 

146 even-indexed ones into radii, and words 0/1 and 2/3 form the two 

147 (cosine, sine) pairs. Both constants are powers of two, so the mapping is 

148 exact. 

149 """ 

150 u1 = tl.fma(r0.to(tl.float32), 2.3283064365386963e-10, 1.1641532182693481e-10) 

151 u2 = tl.fma(r1.to(tl.float32), 2.3283064365386963e-10, 1.1641532182693481e-10) 

152 u3 = tl.fma(r2.to(tl.float32), 2.3283064365386963e-10, 1.1641532182693481e-10) 

153 u4 = tl.fma(r3.to(tl.float32), 2.3283064365386963e-10, 1.1641532182693481e-10) 

154 

155 radius1 = tl.sqrt(-2.0 * tl.log(u1)) 

156 radius2 = tl.sqrt(-2.0 * tl.log(u3)) 

157 theta1 = 6.2831853071795864 * u2 

158 theta2 = 6.2831853071795864 * u4 

159 

160 return ( 

161 radius1 * tl.cos(theta1), 

162 radius1 * tl.sin(theta1), 

163 radius2 * tl.cos(theta2), 

164 radius2 * tl.sin(theta2), 

165 ) 

166 

167 

168@triton.jit 

169def _box_muller_f64(r0, r1, r2, r3): 

170 """Pair four Philox words into two standard normals, in float64. 

171 

172 Mirrors ``box_muller_double``: each normal spends two words, packed into 

173 roughly 64 bits of uniform randomness instead of 32, so one Philox call 

174 yields two samples rather than four. 

175 """ 

176 m = 2.3283064365386963e-10 

177 u1 = tl.fma(r0.to(tl.float64), m, r1.to(tl.float64) * m * m + m * m * 0.5) 

178 u2 = tl.fma(r2.to(tl.float64), m, r3.to(tl.float64) * m * m + m * m * 0.5) 

179 

180 radius = tl.sqrt(-2.0 * tl.log(u1)) 

181 theta = 6.2831853071795864 * u2 

182 

183 return radius * tl.cos(theta), radius * tl.sin(theta) 

184 

185 

186@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["n_elem", "num_prog"]) 

187def _philox_normal_gcu400( 

188 out_ptr, 

189 key_ptr, 

190 n_elem, 

191 mean, 

192 std, 

193 num_prog, 

194 BLOCK: tl.constexpr, 

195 EVEN: tl.constexpr, 

196 PERSIST: tl.constexpr, 

197): 

198 """Fill ``out_ptr`` with normal samples from a stateless Philox stream. 

199 

200 Element ``i`` comes from the ``i // 4``-th Philox 4x32 counter value 

201 (counter = offset + i // 4, subsequence zero), word ``i % 4``, mapped 

202 through ATen's Box-Muller transform. The 32-bit fast path is taken per 

203 launch via a runtime scalar branch; both branches produce identical 

204 values for the same (seed, offset). 

205 """ 

206 seed = tl.load(key_ptr).to(tl.uint64) 

207 offset = tl.load(key_ptr + 1).to(tl.uint64) 

208 pid = tl.program_id(0) 

209 total_blocks = (n_elem + BLOCK * 4 - 1) // (BLOCK * 4) 

210 # uint32 fast path: the whole counter window and the flat element 

211 # offsets must stay inside 32 bits. Checked on the device because the 

212 # (seed, offset) pair lives in a device tensor; a host-side check would 

213 # sync every call. offset < 2**32 is implied by the first bound. 

214 u32_ok = (n_elem < 0x80000000) & ( 

215 offset + total_blocks.to(tl.uint64) * BLOCK <= 0x100000000 

216 ) 

217 dtype = out_ptr.dtype.element_ty 

218 if PERSIST: 

219 if u32_ok: 

220 for block_idx in range(pid, total_blocks, num_prog): 

221 chunks = block_idx * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK).to(tl.uint32) 

222 c0 = offset.to(tl.uint32) + chunks 

223 z = c0 * 0 

224 r0, r1, r2, r3 = tl.philox(seed, c0, z, z, z) 

225 n0, n1, n2, n3 = _box_muller_f32(r0, r1, r2, r3) 

226 v0 = tl.fma(n0, std, mean).to(dtype) 

227 v1 = tl.fma(n1, std, mean).to(dtype) 

228 v2 = tl.fma(n2, std, mean).to(dtype) 

229 v3 = tl.fma(n3, std, mean).to(dtype) 

230 base = chunks * 4 

231 if EVEN: 

232 tl.store(out_ptr + base, v0) 

233 tl.store(out_ptr + base + 1, v1) 

234 tl.store(out_ptr + base + 2, v2) 

235 tl.store(out_ptr + base + 3, v3) 

236 else: 

237 n32 = n_elem.to(tl.uint32) 

238 tl.store(out_ptr + base, v0, mask=base < n32) 

239 tl.store(out_ptr + base + 1, v1, mask=base + 1 < n32) 

240 tl.store(out_ptr + base + 2, v2, mask=base + 2 < n32) 

241 tl.store(out_ptr + base + 3, v3, mask=base + 3 < n32) 

242 else: 

243 for block_idx in range(pid, total_blocks, num_prog): 

244 chunks64 = block_idx.to(tl.int64) * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK).to( 

245 tl.int64 

246 ) 

247 counter = offset + chunks64.to(tl.uint64) 

248 c0 = (counter & 0xFFFFFFFF).to(tl.uint32) 

249 c1 = ((counter >> 32) & 0xFFFFFFFF).to(tl.uint32) 

250 z = c0 * 0 

251 r0, r1, r2, r3 = tl.philox(seed, c0, c1, z, z) 

252 n0, n1, n2, n3 = _box_muller_f32(r0, r1, r2, r3) 

253 base64 = chunks64 * 4 

254 tl.store( 

255 out_ptr + base64, 

256 tl.fma(n0, std, mean).to(dtype), 

257 mask=base64 < n_elem, 

258 ) 

259 tl.store( 

260 out_ptr + base64 + 1, 

261 tl.fma(n1, std, mean).to(dtype), 

262 mask=base64 + 1 < n_elem, 

263 ) 

264 tl.store( 

265 out_ptr + base64 + 2, 

266 tl.fma(n2, std, mean).to(dtype), 

267 mask=base64 + 2 < n_elem, 

268 ) 

269 tl.store( 

270 out_ptr + base64 + 3, 

271 tl.fma(n3, std, mean).to(dtype), 

272 mask=base64 + 3 < n_elem, 

273 ) 

274 else: 

275 if u32_ok: 

276 chunks = pid * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK).to(tl.uint32) 

277 c0 = offset.to(tl.uint32) + chunks 

278 z = c0 * 0 

279 r0, r1, r2, r3 = tl.philox(seed, c0, z, z, z) 

280 n0, n1, n2, n3 = _box_muller_f32(r0, r1, r2, r3) 

281 v0 = tl.fma(n0, std, mean).to(dtype) 

282 v1 = tl.fma(n1, std, mean).to(dtype) 

283 v2 = tl.fma(n2, std, mean).to(dtype) 

284 v3 = tl.fma(n3, std, mean).to(dtype) 

285 base = chunks * 4 

286 if EVEN: 

287 tl.store(out_ptr + base, v0) 

288 tl.store(out_ptr + base + 1, v1) 

289 tl.store(out_ptr + base + 2, v2) 

290 tl.store(out_ptr + base + 3, v3) 

291 else: 

292 n32 = n_elem.to(tl.uint32) 

293 tl.store(out_ptr + base, v0, mask=base < n32) 

294 tl.store(out_ptr + base + 1, v1, mask=base + 1 < n32) 

295 tl.store(out_ptr + base + 2, v2, mask=base + 2 < n32) 

296 tl.store(out_ptr + base + 3, v3, mask=base + 3 < n32) 

297 else: 

298 chunks64 = pid.to(tl.int64) * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK).to(tl.int64) 

299 counter = offset + chunks64.to(tl.uint64) 

300 c0 = (counter & 0xFFFFFFFF).to(tl.uint32) 

301 c1 = ((counter >> 32) & 0xFFFFFFFF).to(tl.uint32) 

302 z = c0 * 0 

303 r0, r1, r2, r3 = tl.philox(seed, c0, c1, z, z) 

304 n0, n1, n2, n3 = _box_muller_f32(r0, r1, r2, r3) 

305 base64 = chunks64 * 4 

306 tl.store( 

307 out_ptr + base64, tl.fma(n0, std, mean).to(dtype), mask=base64 < n_elem 

308 ) 

309 tl.store( 

310 out_ptr + base64 + 1, 

311 tl.fma(n1, std, mean).to(dtype), 

312 mask=base64 + 1 < n_elem, 

313 ) 

314 tl.store( 

315 out_ptr + base64 + 2, 

316 tl.fma(n2, std, mean).to(dtype), 

317 mask=base64 + 2 < n_elem, 

318 ) 

319 tl.store( 

320 out_ptr + base64 + 3, 

321 tl.fma(n3, std, mean).to(dtype), 

322 mask=base64 + 3 < n_elem, 

323 )

326@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["n_elem", "num_prog"]) 

327def _philox_normal_f64_gcu400( 

328 out_ptr, 

329 key_ptr, 

330 params_ptr, 

331 n_elem, 

332 num_prog, 

333 BLOCK: tl.constexpr, 

334): 

335 """float64 arm: two samples per counter, 64-bit counter math, grid-stride. 

336 

337 ``params_ptr`` addresses a ``(mean, std)`` pair of doubles. They arrive as 

338 a device tensor rather than Python floats because Triton narrows float 

339 kernel arguments to float32, which would drop the low mantissa bits of an 

340 arbitrary mean/std. Kept for ATen parity; gcu400 has no fp64 arithmetic, 

341 so this kernel is never exercised by the accuracy suite on this target 

342 (fp64 is filtered from the test dtypes). 

343 """ 

344 seed = tl.load(key_ptr).to(tl.uint64) 

345 offset = tl.load(key_ptr + 1).to(tl.uint64) 

346 mean = tl.load(params_ptr) 

347 std = tl.load(params_ptr + 1) 

348 pid = tl.program_id(0) 

349 total_blocks = (n_elem + BLOCK * 2 - 1) // (BLOCK * 2) 

350 for block_idx in range(pid, total_blocks, num_prog): 

351 chunks = block_idx.to(tl.int64) * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK).to(tl.int64) 

352 counter = offset + chunks.to(tl.uint64) 

353 c0 = (counter & 0xFFFFFFFF).to(tl.uint32) 

354 c1 = ((counter >> 32) & 0xFFFFFFFF).to(tl.uint32) 

355 z = c0 * 0 

356 r0, r1, r2, r3 = tl.philox(seed, c0, c1, z, z) 

357 n0, n1 = _box_muller_f64(r0, r1, r2, r3) 

358 base = chunks * 2 

359 tl.store(out_ptr + base, tl.fma(n0, std, mean), mask=base < n_elem) 

360 tl.store(out_ptr + base + 1, tl.fma(n1, std, mean), mask=base + 1 < n_elem) 

361 

362 

363def _launch(out, key, mean, std): 

364 n = out.numel() 

365 if out.dtype == torch.float64: 

366 # ATen accumulates 8-byte outputs in double, so the parameters are 

367 # cast to double before they reach the kernel. 

368 params = torch.tensor([mean, std], dtype=torch.float64, device=out.device) 

369 # Two elements per Philox call, so each lane covers half as much as in 

370 # the 16/32-bit path. 

371 grid = min(triton.cdiv(n, _F64_BLOCK * 2), _MAX_GRID_X) 

372 with torch_device_fn.device(out.device): 

373 _philox_normal_f64_gcu400[(grid,)]( 

374 out, 

375 key, 

376 params, 

377 n, 

378 grid, 

379 BLOCK=_F64_BLOCK, 

380 num_warps=4, 

381 ) 

382 return 

383 

384 if n <= _SMALL_MAX_NUMEL: 

385 block = _SMALL_BLOCK 

386 grid = triton.cdiv(n, block * 4) 

387 with torch_device_fn.device(out.device): 

388 _philox_normal_gcu400[(grid,)]( 

389 out, 

390 key, 

391 n, 

392 mean, 

393 std, 

394 grid, 

395 BLOCK=block, 

396 EVEN=n % (block * 4) == 0, 

397 PERSIST=False, 

398 num_warps=_SMALL_NUM_WARPS, 

399 ) 

400 return 

401 

402 block = _PERSIST_BLOCK 

403 grid = min(triton.cdiv(n, block * 4), _PERSIST_NUM_PROG) 

404 with torch_device_fn.device(out.device): 

405 _philox_normal_gcu400[(grid,)]( 

406 out, 

407 key, 

408 n, 

409 mean, 

410 std, 

411 grid, 

412 BLOCK=block, 

413 EVEN=n % (block * 4) == 0, 

414 PERSIST=True, 

415 num_warps=_PERSIST_NUM_WARPS, 

416 ) 

417 

418 

419def _check_args(self, key): 

420 if not self.is_floating_point(): 

421 raise RuntimeError( 

422 f"_philox_normal_: self must be a floating point tensor, got {self.dtype}" 

423 ) 

424 if key.dtype != torch.uint64: 

425 raise RuntimeError( 

426 f"_philox_normal_: key must have dtype uint64, got {key.dtype}" 

427 ) 

428 if self.device != key.device: 

429 raise RuntimeError( 

430 f"_philox_normal_: self and key must be on the same device, got " 

431 f"{self.device} and {key.device}" 

432 ) 

433 if key.dim() < 1 or key.size(-1) != 2: 

434 raise RuntimeError( 

435 f"_philox_normal_: key must have shape (2,) or (*batch, 2), got " 

436 f"{tuple(key.shape)}" 

437 ) 

438 if key.dim() > 1 and key.dim() != self.dim() + 1: 

439 raise RuntimeError( 

440 f"_philox_normal_: batched key must have ndim == output ndim + 1, got " 

441 f"key shape {tuple(key.shape)} with output shape {tuple(self.shape)}" 

442 ) 

443 

444 

445def _batched_key_plan(out, key): 

446 """Split a batched key into per-key output blocks and key indices. 

447 

448 ATen derives the elements one key owns by counting the output's trailing 

449 dimensions that the key leaves unsized (``key.size(i) == 1``); a key with 

450 shape ``(4, 1, 1, 2)`` against output ``(4, 10, 100)`` therefore feeds 1000 

451 elements. The remaining key dimensions broadcast, so the key index for a 

452 block is the flat index of a zero-based multi-index along those dims. 

453 """ 

454 elems_per_key = 1 

455 key_dims = out.dim() 

456 for i in range(out.dim() - 1, -1, -1): 

457 if key.size(i) != 1: 

458 break 

459 elems_per_key *= out.size(i) 

460 key_dims -= 1 

461 

462 key_batch = tuple(key.shape[:key_dims]) 

463 out_batch = tuple(out.shape[:key_dims]) 

464 for ks, os_ in zip(key_batch, out_batch): 

465 if ks != os_ and ks != 1: 

466 raise RuntimeError( 

467 f"_philox_normal_: key batch shape {key_batch} is not " 

468 f"broadcastable with output shape {out_batch}" 

469 ) 

470 

471 num_blocks = out.numel() // elems_per_key 

472 # Walk the batch dims in output order, advancing the key's flat index only 

473 # where the key is actually sized (broadcast dims keep their index). 

474 strides = [] 

475 acc = 1 

476 for ks in reversed(key_batch): 

477 strides.append(0 if ks == 1 else acc) 

478 acc *= ks 

479 strides.reverse() 

480 

481 block = [] 

482 for b in range(num_blocks): 

483 idx = 0 

484 rem = b 

485 for dim in range(key_dims - 1, -1, -1): 

486 size = out_batch[dim] 

487 coord = rem % size if size else 0 

488 rem //= size if size else 1 

489 idx += coord * strides[dim] 

490 block.append(idx) 

491 return elems_per_key, block 

492 

493 

494def _philox_normal_(self, key, mean=0.0, std=1.0): 

495 logger.debug("GEMS_ENFLAME_PHILOX_NORMAL_") 

496 _check_args(self, key) 

497 if self.numel() == 0: 

498 return self 

499 

500 key = key.contiguous() 

501 # Non-contiguous outputs are filled through a contiguous staging buffer and 

502 # copied back, so the kernel can rely on plain linear indexing. 

503 contiguous = self.is_contiguous() 

504 out = self if contiguous else self.contiguous() 

505 

506 if key.dim() == 1: 

507 _launch(out, key, mean, std) 

508 else: 

509 elems_per_key, block_keys = _batched_key_plan(out, key) 

510 key_flat = key.reshape(-1, 2) 

511 out_flat = out.reshape(-1, elems_per_key) 

512 for block_idx, key_idx in enumerate(block_keys): 

513 _launch(out_flat[block_idx], key_flat[key_idx], mean, std) 

514 

515 if not contiguous: 

516 self.copy_(out) 

517 return self 

518 

519 

520# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

521# Namespace sync: ``SpecOpRegistrar`` only rebinds the top-level ``flag_gems`` 

522# namespace, so the ``flag_gems.ops._philox_normal_`` submodule attribute -- 

523# the object benchmark/test_philox_normal_.py binds as ``gems_op`` -- keeps 

524# pointing at the generic implementation, whose 1D cdiv(N, 2048) grid 

525# overflows the 65535-program grid.x cap on the 2**30 core shapes 

526# (``OutOfResources: out of resource: grid.x``, P19). Rebind the package 

527# attribute to this specialized host so every reference path (top level, 

528# ATen registration, ops submodule) runs the GCU400 kernel. ``flag_gems.ops`` 

529# is fully imported before the registrar loads this module, so the import 

530# below is a plain sys.modules hit. 

531try: 

532 import flag_gems.ops as _generic_ops_pkg 

533except ImportError: # pragma: no cover - flag_gems.ops always importable 

534 _generic_ops_pkg = None 

535 

536if ( 

537 _generic_ops_pkg is not None 

538 and getattr(_generic_ops_pkg, "_philox_normal_", None) is not _philox_normal_ 

539): 

540 _generic_ops_pkg._philox_normal_ = _philox_normal_
